# Setmore vs. Calendly Alternatives: Which Should You Pick?

Time is money, and scheduling meetings manually can eat up a lot of both.

![Calendar booking software displayed on a tablet beside a notebook and coffee cup on a speckled table](https://framerusercontent.com/images/AKAd2WTG2SL2TY12G8KOG4M9Rjw.webp?width=1536&height=1024)

Time is money, and scheduling meetings manually can eat up a lot of both. For small business owners, freelancers, and even enterprise teams, managing appointments efficiently is crucial for success. Constant back-and-forth emails or phone tag to set up meetings wastes time and can frustrate clients. That's why many companies now turn to [online scheduling tools](https://app.cal.com/signup) (essentially schedule planner apps to streamline the process. These business scheduling apps let clients self-book time slots, send automated confirmations and reminders, and keep everyone's calendars in sync. The benefits are clear – [all appointments are now booked online](http://smbguide.com/) rather than via phone, dramatically reducing the workload on staff.

## [Why Online Scheduling Matters](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#why-online-scheduling-matters)

Adopting an online scheduling system can directly benefit your business’s professionalism, bottom line, and efficiency. By allowing clients to book on their own, you’re essentially keeping your “doors” open 24/7. This increased accessibility often translates into more appointments and higher revenue. Automated scheduling tools also help reduce human error and forgetfulness – for example, reminder notifications can dramatically cut down on no-shows (saving you from lost revenue and wasted time).

Handling bookings online frees up staff from playing phone tag and managing calendars manually. It also creates a more polished experience for your clientele – allowing them to self-book at their convenience reflects well on your professionalism, far more than a series of missed calls or lengthy email threads. In short, using an online scheduler means more bookings with less effort, which is a win-win for both you and your clients. With the rise of remote and hybrid work in recent years, scheduling platforms have become even more indispensable for coordinating virtual meetings across time zones.

![Calendar scheduling in a planner with colorful sticky notes and handwritten reminders at an office desk.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/0AIpuCfXFGPNwGXQDaP7psfneKo.webp?width=1536&height=1024)

## [Setmore: Simple Scheduling for Small Businesses](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#setmore-simple-scheduling-for-small-businesses)

Setmore is often touted as the [best booking system for small business](https://cal.com/enterprise) users who need a straightforward way to let customers book appointments online. It offers a clean, easy-to-use interface with core features like a shareable booking page, calendar sync, automated email reminders, and even built-in payment processing. One of its biggest draws is its free plan – it supports up to 4 staff logins at no cost, which is quite generous compared to many competitors.

This has carved out a niche among small businesses (salons, clinics, consultants) thanks to its simplicity and solid value. Users often praise how easy it is to get started and the professional image it projects to clients. The platform even provides 24/7 live customer support to all users, free or paid. However, that very simplicity can be a double-edged sword. Customization options for the booking page are fairly basic (with limited control over design), and some users report minor glitches as their scheduling needs grow more complex. [Setmore](http://meetergo.com/) covers the fundamentals well, but power users may find its feature depth limiting as they scale.

For example, a local salon could use this to display a menu of services (haircuts, coloring, etc.) on its online booking page. Clients visiting the page can select the service they need, choose from available time slots with their preferred stylist, and even pay a deposit upfront if required. Once booked, the appointment appears instantly on the salon’s calendar in Setmore, and both client and staff receive confirmations and reminder notifications. By using it in this way, the salon avoids phone tag with customers and ensures that each stylist’s schedule is managed smoothly in one centralized system.

## [Calendly: Power for Professional Scheduling](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#calendly-power-for-professional-scheduling)

Calendly is one of the most popular calendar booking software tools on the market, used by individuals and organizations alike to coordinate meetings. The platform offers a polished experience with seamless integrations (Google and Outlook calendars, Zoom, Slack, CRM systems, and more), plus workflow features that handle booking logistics for you. Its popularity is hard to overstate – as of late 2023, it reportedly serves over [20 million users worldwide](http://research.contrary.com/) across 100,000+ companies. It has become a go-to solution in many corporate environments thanks to its ease of use and reliability.

For a solo user, Calendly makes it simple to set up a personal booking link and eliminate the back-and-forth emails when scheduling. Teams benefit from advanced options like round-robin assignments and routing forms that automatically direct appointments to the right team member. Its basic version is free and provides unlimited one-on-one event scheduling, but it does have some limitations – for example, a free user can only offer one meeting type at a time. To unlock more, you’ll need a paid plan. Their paid tiers allow multiple event types, pooled team calendars, customizable email/text reminders, and other premium features. Calendly is a robust, mature scheduling solution geared toward professional use. It excels at handling volume and complexity: recruiters use it to coordinate interviews, sales teams use it to schedule demos, and customer success teams use it to book support calls. The trade-off is that some of these premium capabilities come at a cost, and as your team grows, the subscription fees can add up. Still, many consider it the benchmark among scheduling platforms for business for its automation and broad integration support.

## [Setmore and Calendly: Typical Use Cases and Industries Served](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#setmore-and-calendly-typical-use-cases-and-industries-served)

When evaluating online scheduling tools like Setmore and Calendly, it’s essential to understand the types of businesses and scenarios where each platform truly excels. Both tools aim to automate appointment booking and eliminate the hassle of manual scheduling, but their design philosophies and feature sets have led them to serve somewhat different audiences and industries. Setmore is popular with appointment-based B2C businesses like salons, spas, clinics, and fitness studios for its easy-to-use interface and generous free plan. It lets clients book services, choose staff, and pay online, making it ideal for small teams. Features like automated reminders, staff scheduling, and integrations with website builders and social media help businesses manage appointments and connect with customers efficiently.

Calendly, on the other hand, is widely adopted in the B2B (business-to-business) sector and among professionals who need to coordinate a high volume of meetings—both internally and externally. Its user base spans sales teams scheduling demos, recruiters coordinating interviews, consultants organizing client calls, and customer success teams booking support sessions. Calendly’s strengths lie in its seamless calendar integrations, robust automation, and advanced routing features, making it ideal for organizations that juggle multiple meeting types and participants. For example, a sales team might use Calendly’s round-robin assignment to distribute inbound demo requests evenly among team members, or a recruiting department might leverage its integration with Zoom and Google Calendar to streamline candidate interviews. Calendly’s popularity in corporate environments is also driven by its compatibility with a wide array of workplace tools—such as Slack, HubSpot, Salesforce, and Microsoft Teams—enabling it to fit neatly into complex business workflows. Even solo professionals, like coaches or consultants, benefit from Calendly’s ability to automate scheduling, reduce email back-and-forth, and present a polished, professional image to clients.

### [Distinction Between B2B and B2C Use Cases](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#distinction-between-b2b-and-b2c-use-cases)

When comparing Setmore and Calendly, it's important to consider if your business is B2B or B2C, as this affects which platform fits best. Setmore is ideal for B2C service businesses like salons, gyms, and tutoring centers, offering easy booking, staff scheduling, customer management, and payment processing. It helps these businesses provide a smooth customer experience and reduce manual work, with integrations for websites and social media. Calendly is built for B2B needs, supporting teams that coordinate meetings such as sales demos, interviews, and client calls. It integrates with tools like Slack, Salesforce, and Zoom, offering features like round-robin scheduling, team availability, and automation to handle complex meeting workflows efficiently. Choosing the right platform depends on whether your business serves consumers or other businesses: Setmore suits customer-focused services, while Calendly is best for teams managing professional meetings.

## [Setmore vs. Calendly](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#setmore-vs-calendly)

Both Setmore and Calendly aim to simplify scheduling, but they have notable differences in features, pricing, and focus. Here’s how these two scheduling platforms for business compare:

- **Pricing:** Setmore’s paid plans are generally more budget-friendly for small teams. The Pro plan costs about $12/month total, and the Team plan is around $9 per user/month, and even the free tier supports multiple staff. Calendly’s core paid plans run roughly $10–$15 per user/month, which can add up for larger teams. Setmore’s free tier is generous (multiple staff accounts and services), but it lacks two-way calendar syncing until you upgrade. Calendly’s free plan, in contrast, includes 2-way calendar sync out-of-the-box but restricts you to one active event type until you pay. In other words, Setmore gives you more flexibility with appointment types for free, while Calendly gives you more calendar connectivity for free.

- **Team Scheduling:** Calendly is built with team coordination in mind – paid plans support round-robin distribution, pooled availability, and other group scheduling features ideal for sales or support teams. Setmore, on the other hand, is more oriented toward individual calendars; it lacks advanced team routing (you can have multiple staff profiles, but no automated round-robin assignments).

- **Payment & Booking Features:** Both tools allow accepting payments for appointments, but Setmore has an edge for small businesses here. Setmore integrates with Stripe, Square, and PayPal so clients can pay at booking, which is great for appointments like consultations or classes. Calendly offers payment integration only on its paid plans.

- **Integrations & Ecosystem:** Calendly offers a wider range of direct integrations with workplace tools and a robust API, reflecting its focus on professional workflows. Setmore covers the basics and can integrate through Zapier for other needs. Both platforms are accessible via a web browser and offer mobile apps for managing schedules on the go. Setmore even provides a desktop application for Windows, whereas Calendly offers handy browser extensions that let you schedule meetings directly from your email or website.

- **Use Case Fit:** In summary, Setmore is an all-in-one appointment hub ideal for a small service business that wants scheduling, plus customer management and payments in one package. Calendly, by contrast, is tailored more for meeting scheduling at scale – it's often preferred by professionals and larger teams who need advanced scheduling automation and integration into their broader business processes.


Comparing Setmore and Calendly side by side reveals which scheduling tool suits your needs. Both simplify appointment booking, but Setmore is ideal for small businesses with its free plan, which allows up to four staff, unlimited appointments, a branded booking page, service menus, staff assignments, payment processing, and automated reminders. Its customer database and 24/7 support make it especially user-friendly for service providers. In contrast, Calendly’s feature set is tailored for professionals and teams who need more advanced scheduling automation and integration. Even the free plan offers robust calendar syncing and unlimited one-on-one meetings, but it restricts users to a single meeting type and calendar connection unless upgraded. Paid Calendly plans unlock powerful features such as round-robin scheduling, pooled team availability, workflow automations, and advanced routing logic—allowing organizations to direct booking requests to the right team member based on custom forms.

![Top scheduling tools represented by a hand writing in a May 2021 desk calendar beside coffee and stationery.](https://framerusercontent.com/images/XRkab8mF3EUrqXO8h36QvWdBU.webp?width=1536&height=1024)

Calendly also excels in integration breadth, supporting over 100 native connections with workplace tools like Slack, Salesforce, HubSpot, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams, making it ideal for sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that rely on seamless workflows. Unique to Calendly are features like meeting polls (letting invitees vote on times), multi-calendar sync, and detailed analytics dashboards. Setmore offers unique features like social media booking, customer reviews on booking pages, and managing multiple appointments at once—options not available in Calendly. However, it has fewer customization options and some advanced features require workarounds. Setmore suits small service businesses wanting simplicity and affordable scheduling, while Calendly is better for larger teams needing advanced automation and integrations. Comparing their strengths helps businesses choose the right fit for their scheduling needs.

## [Pricing and Plans: Setmore vs. Calendly](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#pricing-and-plans-setmore-vs-calendly)

When choosing an online scheduling tool, understanding the pricing structure and what you get at each tier is crucial—especially as your business grows or your scheduling needs become more complex. Here’s a breakdown of how Setmore and Calendly structure their plans, what’s included, and where each delivers the most value.

### [Setmore Pricing and Value](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#setmore-pricing-and-value)

If you're considering Setmore as your appointment scheduling platform, it's important to understand the different plans and their features. Below is an overview of Setmore's pricing options and what makes each plan unique.

- **Free Plan:** Setmore’s free plan is one of the most generous available for small businesses. It supports up to four users at no cost, allowing unlimited appointments and providing essential features like a branded booking page, automated email reminders, and payment processing via Square. This makes it an excellent option for salons, clinics, consultants, or any service-based business that needs scheduling for multiple staff without upfront costs.

- **Pro Plan:** For $12 per user per month (for one or two users), the Pro plan unlocks additional features such as two-way calendar sync (with Google and Office 365), SMS reminders, and advanced integrations. This plan is ideal if you need more robust calendar management or want to reduce no-shows with text notifications.

- **Team Plan:** If you have a larger team, Setmore’s Team plan is $9 per user per month for unlimited users. It includes all Pro features, making it a scalable and cost-effective solution for growing businesses that need to manage multiple staff schedules efficiently.

- **Value Proposition:** Setmore stands out for its free multi-user support, built-in payment processing (even on the free plan), and 24/7 live customer support for all users. Its pricing is especially attractive for small teams or service providers who want a straightforward, affordable way to manage appointments without sacrificing essential features.


Whether you're just starting out or managing a large team, you can find a plan that fits your needs and budget while benefiting from robust scheduling features and reliable customer support.

### [Calendly Pricing and Value](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#calendly-pricing-and-value)

Calendly’s free plan is ideal for solo users or very small teams, offering unlimited one-on-one event scheduling and two-way calendar sync with Google, Office 365, and iCloud. However, it only allows one active event type and one connected calendar per user, which can be restrictive if you manage multiple services or appointment types. For greater flexibility, it provides paid plans that start at $12 per user per month for the Standard plan and $20 per user per month for the Teams plan. These plans support multiple event types, pooled team availability, advanced workflow automations, customizable reminders, and expanded integrations, including payment options. The Teams plan adds admin controls and advanced scheduling features for larger organizations. For organizations with 30 or more users, the Enterprise plan offers custom pricing, enhanced security, and priority support. Calendly stands out for its user-friendly interface, robust integration ecosystem, and automation features that help professionals and teams save time. While the free plan is limited, the paid options deliver advanced scheduling capabilities, team coordination tools, and seamless integration with workplace software.

### [Cost Implications and Choosing the Right Fit](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#cost-implications-and-choosing-the-right-fit)

Setmore is ideal if you want a cost-effective solution for a small team, need free payment processing, and value strong customer support. Its pricing model is friendly for businesses that want to avoid per-user fees as they grow. Calendly is a better fit if your scheduling needs are complex, you require advanced automation or integrations, or you’re part of a larger team where workflow efficiency is critical—just be mindful that costs can scale quickly with more users. Evaluating your team size, the features you need, and your budget, you can choose the platform that delivers the best value for your specific business scenario. Both tools offer a free starting point, so you can try them out before committing to a paid plan.

## [User Feedback and Reviews](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#user-feedback-and-reviews)

What do actual users think of these tools? By and large, both Setmore and Calendly receive very positive reviews from their customers on major software platforms. [Calendly](http://calendesk.com/) is often praised for being efficient, easy to use, and integrating smoothly with calendars and video meeting tools – though a few users note it can crash occasionally or wish it offered more advanced functionality out of the box. Setmore users love the ability to tailor services and frequently commend the responsive customer support, but some have experienced minor issues with managing multiple staff accounts or needing workarounds for certain advanced needs. In short, both tools have very satisfied user bases, with only relatively small shortcomings reported given the time-saving benefits they provide.

## [Alternatives to Setmore and Calendly](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#alternatives-to-setmore-and-calendly)

When evaluating setmore alternatives or apps like Calendly, you’ll find plenty of capable competitors that might align even better with your needs. Here are a few popular options to consider:

- **Acuity Scheduling (Squarespace Scheduling):** Acuity is known for its advanced customization and client management features. It’s great for appointment-based businesses that want to embed booking forms on their website, set up intake questionnaires, and brand the entire scheduling experience. Many consultants, wellness providers, and salons use Acuity for its rich features.

- **Doodle:** Doodle specializes in coordinating group meetings. It allows you to poll participants for their availability and find a common time that works for everyone. If you frequently schedule meetings with multiple external stakeholders or large groups, Doodle can save you countless email threads.

- **Square Appointments:** Offered by Square, this tool integrates scheduling with a point-of-sale system. It’s especially popular among small businesses in retail and beauty. Square Appointments lets you accept bookings online, send automatic reminders, and have clients’ appointments seamlessly tied to inventory and payment processing in the Square POS.

- **Other Noteworthy Tools:** There are many other options as well. For example,YouCanBook.me provides a simple booking page that syncs with your Google or Outlook calendar, and newer tools like SavvyCal focus on a more collaborative scheduling experience, while others, such asSimplyBook.me, Appointlet, or Bookafy target specific niches. If you have unique requirements or operate in a specific industry, you may find a platform tailored to your use case.

- [**Cal.com**](https://app.cal.com/signup) **(Open-Source):** One modern alternative gaining attention is [Cal.com](https://app.cal.com/signup). Unlike the above proprietary services, this is an open-source scheduling platform that gives you full control over your booking system. It offers a developer-friendly approach – you can self-host it or extend it with custom plugins and integrations. [Cal.com](https://app.cal.com/signup)’s free tier is remarkably feature-rich: users get unlimited event types, multi-calendar syncing, team scheduling, and custom branding with no per-user fees. Thanks to this flexibility, some reviewers have called this _“by far the best meeting scheduler”_ for individuals, startups, and even enterprise teams. Essentially, [Cal.com](https://app.cal.com/signup) aims to provide the power of a top-tier scheduler (like Calendly) while avoiding the common limitations, making it a compelling choice if you want a highly customizable online scheduling software solution.


## [Key Features to Evaluate](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#key-features-to-evaluate)

If you’re still unsure, it may help to outline your requirements and compare them against what each platform offers. Consider the following factors when evaluating scheduling software:

- **Calendar Sync & Time Zones:** Does the tool sync in real-time with your primary calendar (Google, Outlook, etc.) and handle time zone differences smoothly? This is crucial to avoid double-bookings and confusion for international meetings.

- **Appointment Types & Customization:** Can you set up the specific meeting or service types you need (different durations, locations, etc.)? Look for the ability to customize your booking page with your branding, and embed it on your website if needed. Check if the software automatically sends email and/or SMS reminders to participants. Timely reminders can dramatically reduce no-shows and improve the overall experience.

- **Team Scheduling Capabilities:** If you work with a team, consider features like round-robin assignment, pooled availability, and admin controls to manage multiple calendars/users.

- **Integrations & Extensions:** Think about what other tools you use (CRM, email marketing, video conferencing, etc.) and check if the scheduling software has direct integrations or API access to connect with your workflow. A strong integration ecosystem can save you time by automating follow-ups, updating records, and more.

- **Pricing & Scalability:** Finally, weigh the cost relative to the features and number of users. A free or low-cost solution might cover you now, but if you plan to grow, examine how the pricing scales for additional team members or advanced features. Also, note any limits (like number of bookings per month or features behind higher tiers) that might affect you down the line.


By keeping these factors in mind, you can make a more informed decision about which calendar scheduling app will serve your business best.

## [Clarifying the Essentials](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#clarifying-the-essentials)

When considering online scheduling tools like Setmore and Calendly, it’s natural to have questions about how they work, what features they offer, and which types of users they best serve. Below are some of the most common questions prospective users ask, along with clear answers to help you decide which platform might be the better fit for your needs.

### [Is Setmore or Calendly better for small businesses?](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#is-setmore-or-calendly-better-for-small-businesses)

Both platforms are popular among small businesses. Setmore is often preferred for its free plan, which supports up to four staff members and unlimited appointments, making it ideal for salons, clinics, and consultants seeking affordable booking solutions. Calendly's free plan allows only one event type and calendar connection unless upgraded. For solo professionals or very small teams needing strong calendar syncing and integrations, Calendly’s free tier may suffice. However, Setmore’s multi-user support and built-in payment processing make it especially appealing for service-oriented businesses.

### [Can I accept payments through these platforms?](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#can-i-accept-payments-through-these-platforms)

Yes, both Setmore and Calendly support payments for appointments, but with key differences. Setmore integrates with Stripe, Square, and PayPal, and even allows Square payments on its free plan, simplifying payment collection at booking. Calendly’s payment integration, available only on paid plans, works with Stripe and PayPal. If you need free payment collection, Setmore is the more accessible choice.

![Meeting scheduler apps shown on a smartphone with a weekly task management interface](https://framerusercontent.com/images/Ilp4b2ghyTYrfWaqTSvkvbD0cA.webp?width=1536&height=1024)

### [Do these tools integrate with other business software?](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#do-these-tools-integrate-with-other-business-software)

Calendly excels in integrations, supporting over 100 native connections with tools like Google and Outlook calendars, Zoom, Slack, and CRM systems. Setmore covers essentials like calendar sync, video conferencing, and payment processors, and can access more apps via Zapier, but has fewer native integrations. For extensive business app connections, Calendly is usually the better option. Setmore’s simplicity can be a double-edged sword: while it’s easy to use, it may lack advanced features needed by larger teams or businesses with complex scheduling requirements. Some users note occasional glitches or the need for workarounds when managing multiple staff or services. Calendly, meanwhile, is highly scalable but locks many advanced features—such as multiple event types, pooled team calendars, and custom notifications—behind its paid tiers. Additionally, some users wish for more flexibility in event management and branding on the free plan.

### [Is customer support available?](https://cal.com/blog/setmore-vs-calendly-alternatives-which-should-you-pick\#is-customer-support-available)

Setmore provides 24/7 live customer support to all users, which is a significant advantage, especially for small businesses that may need help during off-hours. Calendly offers customer support primarily to paid users, so free users have limited access to live assistance. By addressing these frequently asked questions, you can better understand the practical strengths and possible limitations of Setmore and Calendly. Whether you prioritize cost, payment processing, integrations, or support, clarifying these points will help you select the scheduling tool that aligns best with your business needs.

When evaluating Setmore and Calendly, prospective users often have practical questions that go beyond basic features or pricing, focusing instead on real-world concerns that impact day-to-day operations. A frequent question is about data privacy and security—users want to know how their client data is protected, whether the platforms comply with regulations like GDPR, and if sensitive information (such as payment details) is encrypted both in transit and at rest. Both Setmore and Calendly employ standard security protocols, but it’s essential to review their privacy policies and, if you’re in a regulated industry, check for compliance certifications. Another common concern is the ease of migration: many businesses already use another scheduling tool or manage appointments manually, so they want to know if Setmore or Calendly offers import tools or onboarding support to transfer existing contacts, appointments, and settings without disruption. Both platforms provide basic import options (typically via CSV files), but more complex migrations may require manual adjustments or assistance from support.

Mobile app functionality is also a top concern, especially for service providers who work on the go. Prospective users want to know if they can manage bookings, send reminders, and view their calendars from a smartphone or tablet. Both Setmore and Calendly offer mobile apps for iOS and Android, but the depth of functionality can vary; for instance, some advanced features or integrations may only be accessible via the web interface. Lastly, users often ask about booking or user limits, particularly on free plans. For example, Setmore’s free plan supports up to four users and unlimited appointments, but restricts certain integrations and advanced notifications. Calendly’s free tier allows unlimited one-on-one meetings but only supports a single event type and calendar connection per user.

By considering the size of your operation, your feature requirements, and your budget, you can determine which scheduling platform aligns best with your needs. The good news is that all of these tools aim to eliminate the headaches of manual scheduling – whichever you pick, you’ll be saving time and providing a better booking experience to your clients or colleagues. And since all three solutions offer free plans or trial periods, you can test-drive each one's interface and features to see which feels most comfortable for you before committing. Adopting good scheduling apps means less hassle for everyone involved – and more time for you to focus on what really matters in your business.

# Setting up minimum notice period in scheduling

A minimum notice period is like a gentle buffer between the moment someone clicks “book” and when the meeting actually takes place. It's the scheduling equivalent of hitting snooze on an alarm clock, just enough time to get your act together.

In this article, we'll dive into the magic of setting up a minimum notice period, the challenges it solves, and how Cal.com makes it all a breeze. By the end, you'll be booking smarter, not harder.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/EUp1YB2ScPQdQlxpGvWvjg4Tyw.png?width=4000&height=2380)

## [What is a minimum notice period in scheduling apps?](https://cal.com/blog/setting-up-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling\#what-is-a-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling-apps)

You know that moment when you get a last-minute meeting request, and it feels like someone just threw a grenade into your perfectly planned day? Yeah, that’s what we’re avoiding here.

In scheduling apps, a minimum notice period is the amount of time you require before a meeting or appointment can be booked. This period ensures that you have adequate time to prepare before any engagement takes place. For example, if you set a minimum notice of 2 hours, a potential attendee cannot book a meeting with you unless they schedule it at least 2 hours in advance. This simple setting helps prevent last-minute scheduling. Whether you’re a solo entrepreneur, a small team, or a growing organization, having this safeguard is crucial. It gives you that extra time to breathe, prep, and actually make sure you’re ready to knock the meeting out of the park.

## [Common challenges faced without a minimum notice period](https://cal.com/blog/setting-up-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling\#common-challenges-faced-without-a-minimum-notice-period)

Without a minimum notice period, your schedule becomes a game of whack-a-mole. And let’s be honest, no one enjoys playing that game.

- **Last-minute chaos**: Trying to prepare for a meeting that’s about to start in 30 minutes? You may as well be preparing for a surprise party that no one told you about.

- **Overbooking**: We’ve all double-booked ourselves at least once. It’s like when you promise to go to two events on the same day and forget you’ve already RSVP'd. Oops!

- **Burnout**: That “go-go-go” feeling without proper breaks between meetings can wear you out faster than your phone battery on 1% during a 3-hour video call.

- **Unpredictability**: Not knowing when meetings will pop up can make your day feel like it’s constantly out of control.


By setting a minimum notice period, you’re essentially taking back control over your calendar and stopping the madness before it starts.

## [How to set up a minimum notice period in Cal.com](https://cal.com/blog/setting-up-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling\#how-to-set-up-a-minimum-notice-period-in-cal-com)

Setting up a minimum notice period in Cal.com is quick and simple. Here’s a step-by-step guide on how to set it up in your Cal.com account:

1. **Log into Cal.com**

First, [create a Cal.com account](https://app.cal.com/signup) or [log into your existing account](https://app.cal.com/auth/login).

2. **Create a new event type (or select an existing one)**

On the [event types dashboard](https://app.cal.com/event-types), click on '+ New' to create a new event type, or select an existing one if you want to add a notice period to an already created event.

3. **Click on the 'limits' tab**

On the left menu of the event type, click on the 'limits' tab to access the minimum notice feature.

4. **Add a minimum notice time period**

Set up the minimum notice time period by adding a number value in the input field and selecting whether it’s in minutes, hours, or days. For example, if you want a 2-hour notice period, input '2' and select 'hours.'

5. **Save your event type and preview your changes**

Don’t forget to save your event type. You can click on the preview button to see the feature live in action. If set up properly, you won’t be able to schedule a meeting within the set minimum notice time period.


Once you're done, your calendar will automatically reflect the minimum notice requirement, ensuring that every meeting is scheduled with ample preparation time.

## [Benefits of setting a minimum notice period](https://cal.com/blog/setting-up-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling\#benefits-of-setting-a-minimum-notice-period)

Think of the minimum notice period as your new best friend in the world of scheduling. Here’s why:

- **Time to prep**: Whether it’s gathering your notes, getting your coffee, or simply breathing, having extra time ensures you’re ready to go when the meeting starts.

- **Better time management**: You won’t find yourself frantically moving between meetings or looking at your calendar in disbelief that the next event is already here.

- **Professionalism**: A well-structured booking process helps you maintain a polished image, showing clients and colleagues you’re in control and respect your own time.

- **Fewer scheduling disasters**: No more double-booking or scrambling to fit someone into your packed schedule. It’s all about balance.


## [Closing takeaways of setting a minimum notice period in your scheduling app](https://cal.com/blog/setting-up-minimum-notice-period-in-scheduling\#closing-takeaways-of-setting-a-minimum-notice-period-in-your-scheduling-app)

By setting up a minimum notice period, you gain better control over your schedule, reduce the chaos of last-minute meetings, and ensure you're prepared for each event. With Cal.com, implementing and managing these settings is a breeze, so you can focus on what matters most: making an impact in your meetings.

# Simplify Scheduling and Communication with Cal.com’s Skype Integration

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/QP95OAFtRyqXvwg3XpqLsihU.jpg?width=1280&height=853)

## [Prioritizing meaningful meetings](https://cal.com/blog/simplify-scheduling-and-communication-with-cal-com-s-skype-integration\#prioritizing-meaningful-meetings)

When it comes to calendar scheduling, Cal.com does things differently. We're focused on helping people connect and truly own their time; effortless bookings are just a bonus. We know that one calendar scheduling solution isn't going to fit all unless it can be tailored, and we know that what you need might change on a day-to-day basis.

## [Customization for your unique needs](https://cal.com/blog/simplify-scheduling-and-communication-with-cal-com-s-skype-integration\#customization-for-your-unique-needs)

This is why Cal.com's free plan is packed with best-in-class features that you're won't find at the same price point anywhere else. All Cal.com users have options for [analytics](https://cal.com/apps/categories/analytics) integration, [monetization](https://cal.com/apps/categories/payment), and we don't place arbitrary limits on the number of calendar connections or active meeting types that you can have. We want our users to be comfortable in their calendar scheduling environment.

## [Empowering user choices](https://cal.com/blog/simplify-scheduling-and-communication-with-cal-com-s-skype-integration\#empowering-user-choices)

We want you to be able to make the choices that matter to you, and we want to ensure that once you've made those choices, it's easy for you to take action and execute plans based upon them. This is one of the reasons why we've taken the time to truly invest in Cal.com's hosted product. Yes, we're an open-source project and an open startup, but we also know that the majority of our users aren't coders.

This is why we offer advanced granule-level controls via your account settings page as well as multiple dashboards like your events, bookings, and availability dashboard. This helps to ensure that everyone has access to advanced customization options.

## [The good news](https://cal.com/blog/simplify-scheduling-and-communication-with-cal-com-s-skype-integration\#the-good-news)

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/xTpCuM35aacpWugJgKgaCPbg3Ug.jpeg?width=1064&height=696)

[Skype](https://cal.com/apps/skype) has been around for a long time. For many people, it was the first global teleconferencing product that they encountered. It's allowed people to build businesses, reconnect with family, and maintain effective communication lines, no matter where they are.

This is why we are happy to announce that Cal now has a built-in integration for Skype. This is fantastic for anyone who's not only fond of this product but finds it to be an essential component of the way they work.

## [Installing the Skype integration](https://cal.com/blog/simplify-scheduling-and-communication-with-cal-com-s-skype-integration\#installing-the-skype-integration)

To install our app for Skype, follow these steps:

1. Visit the App Store

2. Select the [conferencing](https://cal.com/apps/categories/conferencing) category

3. Scroll down until you find Skype

4. Click on the Details button

5. Click on the Install App button

6. Choose an event to connect to Skype (or select "Set Up Later")


As you can see, adding Skype to your Cal.com teleconferencing options is a simple and straightforward process. Once you've completed the steps above, you can start sharing your booking link and communicating with those who matter most to you on the platform you both enjoy. If you'd like to learn more about our various teleconferencing options, please feel free to check out the conferencing category within our app store.

Thank you for taking the time to read this article. We hope you're enjoying your Cal.com experience and, as always, happy scheduling.

# SMS workflows for automated SMS notifications

SMS workflows have emerged as a game-changer. By automating text message notifications and reminders, businesses can keep their clients and teams informed and engaged without manual effort. This article explores what SMS workflows are, how they can be integrated into scheduling apps, and offers practical tips on using them effectively.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/hNjoaeLbDdxMaOsMnjkdCOXYAA.png?width=3000&height=1785)

## [What are SMS workflows?](https://cal.com/blog/sms-workflows-automated-notifications\#what-are-sms-workflows)

SMS workflows are automated sequences of text messages triggered by specific actions or timeframes. These messages help businesses communicate with customers and team members in a variety of ways, including appointment confirmations, reminders, cancellations, and follow-ups. The power of SMS workflows lies in their ability to save time, reduce human error, and improve communication by keeping everyone informed throughout the scheduling process.

SMS workflows typically involve:

- **Automated triggers:** Based on specific events like booking, cancellation, or reminders.

- **Predefined messages:** Messages that can be customized and scheduled in advance.

- **Follow-up sequences:** Automatic follow-ups to ensure no missed communication.

- **Customizable timing:** Messages sent at set intervals, such as reminders sent 24 hours before an appointment.


These workflows streamline the process of keeping your clients and team members in the loop, reducing manual input while improving engagement.

## [How can SMS workflows be used in scheduling apps?](https://cal.com/blog/sms-workflows-automated-notifications\#how-can-sms-workflows-be-used-in-scheduling-apps)

In scheduling apps, SMS workflows streamline appointment management by automating the communication process. With SMS notifications, businesses can ensure that important details are communicated in real time, keeping everyone on track without the need for additional effort.

Here’s how SMS workflows can be applied in scheduling apps:

1. **Before the event starts:** SMS reminders can be sent to clients to ensure they don’t forget their appointments.

2. **When the event is canceled:** If an appointment is canceled, an SMS can immediately inform the invitee, along with options to reschedule.

3. **When a new event is booked:** After a user schedules an event, an SMS confirmation message can be sent to reassure them that their booking was successful.

4. **After the event ends:** SMS follow-ups can be sent requesting feedback or offering additional services.

5. **When an event is rescheduled:** If a scheduled event is moved to a different time, SMS workflows can notify all participants of the change.


With these triggers, SMS workflows help automate the communication process, ensuring that your scheduling system is seamless and your clients are always in the loop.

## [Practical tips and strategies for using SMS workflows in scheduling](https://cal.com/blog/sms-workflows-automated-notifications\#practical-tips-and-strategies-for-using-sms-workflows-in-scheduling)

To maximize the effectiveness of SMS workflows in scheduling, follow these practical tips and strategies:

1. **Use clear, concise messages:** SMS has a character limit, so keep your messages short and to the point.

2. **Personalize messages:** Address clients by their name and tailor the message content to make it more engaging.

3. **Set reminders at optimal times:** For the best results, send reminders at least 24 hours before the event and a final reminder 1 hour before.

4. **Test your workflows:** Before launching, test your workflows to ensure messages are sent at the right times and are triggered correctly.

5. **Monitor and optimize:** After the workflows are live, check the results and adjust them as needed to ensure optimal engagement.


## [How to set up SMS workflows in Cal.com](https://cal.com/blog/sms-workflows-automated-notifications\#how-to-set-up-sms-workflows-in-cal-com)

Setting up SMS workflows in Cal.com is quick and easy. Follow these steps to automate your scheduling communication:

**1\. Log in to Cal.com**

[Create](https://app.cal.com/signup) an account or [log in](https://app.cal.com/auth/login) to your Cal.com account.

**2\. Navigate to Workflows**

In the left panel of your dashboard, click on **Workflows**.

**3\. Create a new workflow**

Click on the **\+ New** button to create a new workflow. Then, select **Start from Scratch** to build your workflow from the ground up.

**4\. Set up the trigger**

- Click on **When this trigger happens** and select the trigger event (e.g., "Before the event starts", "When the event is canceled", etc.).

- Choose the timing for when the trigger will occur (e.g., immediately, 24 hours before, etc.).

- Select the event type(s) this workflow should apply to, such as a specific booking or event type.


**5\. Set up the SMS workflow action**

- Click on **Send SMS to attendee**.

- Customize the **Sender ID**, which will be the name or number shown as the sender of the SMS. (Note: Some countries do not allow alphanumeric sender IDs.)

- It’s recommended to toggle on **Make phone number required for booking event** to ensure that a phone number is collected during booking.


**6\. Change the SMS message**

Edit the SMS message to be sent to the attendee. Customize the content as needed, such as confirmation, reminders, or rescheduling notifications.

**7\. Save and Done**

Once you’ve set up the trigger and SMS message, click **Save** to activate your workflow. You’re all set!

With Cal.com’s easy-to-use SMS workflow feature, you can ensure your attendees are kept informed at every step of the scheduling process.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/h9V4drunBIxEwPvtS91m5DH8yNE.png?width=3024&height=1716)

## [Closing takeaways](https://cal.com/blog/sms-workflows-automated-notifications\#closing-takeaways)

SMS workflows are a powerful tool for automating communication in scheduling apps. By sending automated reminders, confirmations, and follow-ups, they help businesses improve engagement, reduce no-shows, and enhance the overall scheduling experience. Whether you’re managing appointments for a small team or an enterprise, SMS workflows make scheduling more efficient and user-friendly.

Ready to get started? Explore how Cal.com’s SMS and WhatsApp workflows can streamline your scheduling process and improve communication with your clients and team.

# Streamline Your Appointment Scheduling with Multiple Availability Options

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/RQbKH8UXX9T7kjWYPIwaZCdrtk.jpg?width=1280&height=853)

## [You deserve customizable scheduling](https://cal.com/blog/streamline-your-appointment-scheduling-with-multiple-availability-options\#you-deserve-customizable-scheduling)

Every Cal.com dashboard looks a little different; this isn't surprising since there are many approaches to appointment setting. Some users have a single bookable event and availability schedule, while others have multiple. When you're starting your calendar scheduling strategy journey, sometimes it can be challenging to figure out how to approach things. This is where our blog comes in. We have product features, tutorials, and articles like this one that provide a little extra information while you get your sea legs.

Today, we’ll be explaining the advantage of using [multiple](https://cal.com/help/en/articles/9929567-multiple-schedules) availability schedules. This is something that might seem a little bit overwhelming at first, but soon it'll make sense.

## [Creating Multiple Availability Schedules](https://cal.com/blog/streamline-your-appointment-scheduling-with-multiple-availability-options\#creating-multiple-availability-schedules)

When you first made your Cal.com account, you were prompted to create an [availability](https://cal.com/help/en/articles/9929489-setting-up-your-availability) schedule. However, this isn't the only availability schedule you can create. You can create as many availability schedules as you need. Even though you will always have one default availability schedule, it can be overridden on an event type basis. Ultimately, what this means is that each of your bookable events can actually have its own separate schedule.

## [Example: Sarah the Investment Consultant](https://cal.com/blog/streamline-your-appointment-scheduling-with-multiple-availability-options\#example-sarah-the-investment-consultant)

Let's go over a couple of examples of how this could work. Let's start by imagining a user named Sarah. Sarah is self-employed. She uses Cal.com to book meetings with her clients. As an investment consultant, Sarah offers three primary booking types. She has one event type for regular clients, another event type for speaking engagements, and a third bookable event for free introductory sessions.

## [Sarah's Scheduling Preferences](https://cal.com/blog/streamline-your-appointment-scheduling-with-multiple-availability-options\#sarah-s-scheduling-preferences)

Now, Sarah likes to organize her calendar in a specific way; she prefers to do all introductory work on Mondays and Tuesdays. Sarah also wants to offer the maximum [availability](https://cal.com/blog/using-custom-availability-scheduling) for bookings to her regular clients, so she wants to ensure they have access to her throughout the working week. Sarah also loves public speaking, but she really only has time for that towards the end of the week and during part of the weekend.

With this in mind, Sarah has created several availability schedules. Her main availability schedule runs Monday through Friday, and it's for meetings with her regular clients. Her secondary availability schedule is Fridays and Saturdays, and it's for speaking engagements. Finally, Sarah's third availability schedule is Mondays and Tuesdays, and it's when she does all of her introductory free sessions.

Having three different availability schedules, each for a different appointment type, makes a big difference for Sarah. It means that not only is she able to offer a wide variety of appointment slots, but she's still able to protect her own sense of equilibrium by ensuring that specific bookings only happen on specific days. This keeps things simple and means Sarah is always prepared for the week ahead. The use of multiple availability schedules means that Sarah knows the following will always occur:

- New clients will only have sessions on Mondays and Tuesdays.

- Regular clients will have maximum choice availability running Mondays through Fridays.

- All public speaking gigs will happen on Fridays and Saturdays.


Not everyone is Sarah; some people don't need three availability schedules, but that doesn't mean they can't benefit from two. In the next section, we're going to look at a scenario where a user only has two event types. The first event type is going to be their primary event type and is synced to their default availability schedule. The second event type is a minor event type—it's not the majority of their business; however, it benefits from having its own availability schedule.

## [Ben's Scheduling Strategy](https://cal.com/blog/streamline-your-appointment-scheduling-with-multiple-availability-options\#ben-s-scheduling-strategy)

Meet Ben; he's a fantastic barber. He's respected and well-known—in fact, people travel from other communities to get their haircuts from him. Ben offers two booking types: one is for regular haircuts, and the other is reserved for sensory-friendly haircuts. About 20% of Ben's bookings are for these haircuts, and they require a specific setup. Ben has found that it's most efficient to do all of his sensory haircuts on Thursday.

This means that he's able to provide specialty clients with an environment that they're comfortable in, while also simplifying his own workflow. With this in mind, Ben has created two availability schedules. His main availability schedule is for his regular clientele. This availability schedule runs Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday. This is the schedule that his main bookable event type pulls from.

Ben's secondary availability schedule is connected to the sensory-friendly bookings, and it only offers time slots on Thursday.

Both of Ben's availability schedules are synced to the same calendar. This means that he doesn't have to worry about any double bookings or scheduling errors. It also helps to ensure that all the sensory-friendly appointments are booked on a day when he's able to fully accommodate the needs of the people who book them. This makes it easier for Ben to balance both of his client types so that he can continue to give back without compromising efficiency.

I hope that these two examples have helped to illustrate how custom availability works and the advantages of multiple booking schedules. If you already use this feature and have tips that you'd love to share, give us a shout on [X/Twitter](https://x.com/calcom) and let us know. Thanks for reading, and as always, happy scheduling!

# Streamlining test prep and tutoring businesses with smart scheduling

Test prep and tutoring businesses depend on consistency, flexibility, and personal connection. Cal.com helps streamline it all - from recurring sessions and time zone coordination to group classes and automated reminders.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/qfJJfSoPJhlEXzAgFsYPH2bgJc.png?width=1536&height=1024)

## [The challenge of managing sessions at scale](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#the-challenge-of-managing-sessions-at-scale)

Whether you are running a tutoring agency or working as an independent test prep coach, your day revolves around one thing: time. Managing dozens of student sessions every week means tracking availability, remembering time zones, and making sure no one misses a class.

That is where smart scheduling makes all the difference. Cal.com helps tutors and test prep professionals streamline how sessions are booked, tracked, and delivered.

## [Recurring sessions, without the follow-up](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#recurring-sessions-without-the-follow-up)

Many students preparing for standardized tests like the SAT, GMAT, or TOEFL benefit from weekly or bi-weekly check-ins. But setting up recurring meetings manually can lead to confusion or inconsistency.

With Cal.com, you can set up recurring sessions in just a few clicks. Once a student books the initial time slot, they can opt into a repeating schedule. Each session is automatically confirmed and synced to your calendar, keeping everyone on the same page.

You stay organized. They stay on track.

## [One-on-one bookings across time zones](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#one-on-one-bookings-across-time-zones)

If you tutor students across countries or regions, finding a time that works for everyone is half the battle. Cal.com automatically detects the student’s time zone and adjusts availability accordingly.

This removes the guesswork from international bookings. You set your hours once, and students see options that match their local time. Everyone shows up on time, with no confusion.

## [Group classes made simple](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#group-classes-made-simple)

Running group lessons or workshops? Cal.com makes it easy to schedule and manage sessions with multiple attendees.

You can:

- Create a single booking page for a group session

- Limit the number of seats available

- Allow multiple students to register and receive confirmation


Each student gets calendar invites, reminders, and links to join the session. Whether it is a small study group or a full class, the admin work stays minimal.

## [Stay ahead with automated reminders](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#stay-ahead-with-automated-reminders)

Reminders help reduce no shows and keep students accountable. Cal.com allows you to send automated email and SMS reminders before each session. You decide when they go out and what they say.

This ensures students never forget about a class, and you do not need to chase anyone down.

## [Integrate with your tools](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#integrate-with-your-tools)

Cal.com works with your existing calendar (Google, Outlook, Apple) and integrates with video conferencing platforms like Zoom and Google Meet. Each booking automatically adds the correct video link and blocks off your calendar in real time.

You can also collect payment at the time of booking using Stripe, reducing admin overhead and improving consistency with new students.

## [Built for flexibility](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#built-for-flexibility)

Tutoring is rarely one size fits all. Cal.com is built to adapt:

- Offer different services for different types of prep (math tutoring, essay coaching, diagnostic reviews)

- Customize availability by subject or team member

- Use buffer times between sessions to catch up or prepare


You can even embed your booking page on your website, link it in an email, or include it in your social bio.

## [The bottom line](https://cal.com/blog/streamlining-test-prep-and-tutoring-businesses-with-smart-scheduling\#the-bottom-line)

Smart scheduling is not just about saving time — it is about giving students a better experience and giving tutors more room to focus on what they do best.

With Cal.com, you can manage recurring sessions, set up group classes, handle different time zones, and automate reminders all from one place.

If you are running a tutoring or test prep business and want to reduce no shows, simplify scheduling, and stay fully booked, Cal.com is the tool built for you.

# Efficient appointment booking for tattoo artists: How to manage walk-ins and regulars

Tattoo artists and studio owners are using Cal.com to streamline bookings, accept payments up front, and organize both walk-ins and repeat clients with less stress and more control.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/abUh9n6epsKI1KEzcTXMppxOxJc.png?width=1536&height=1024)

## [The challenge: bookings, walk-ins, and no shows](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#the-challenge-bookings-walk-ins-and-no-shows)

Running a tattoo studio means juggling walk-in requests, planned sessions, and client preferences while staying focused on your craft. But disorganized booking systems, missed appointments, and payment confusion can quickly turn your schedule into chaos.

That is where Cal.com comes in. Tattoo artists and shop managers are using it to simplify appointment scheduling, handle deposits, and offer a smooth experience for both new and returning clients.

## [Bookings that work for you and your clients](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#bookings-that-work-for-you-and-your-clients)

With Cal.com, clients can book based on your real-time availability without any back and forth. You can set up specific appointment types like consultations, flash designs, or multi-hour sessions. Each one can have its own timing, rules, and pricing. Once a booking is confirmed, Cal.com automatically sends out confirmations and reminders to reduce no shows.

Cal.com also supports calendar syncing and built-in buffer times between appointments to keep your day on track.

## [Walk-ins made simple with QR codes](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#walk-ins-made-simple-with-qr-codes)

For studios that accept walk-ins, Cal.com offers an easy solution. Generate a QR code linked to your booking page and display it at your front desk or window.

A walk-in client can scan the code, view your availability, and book the next open slot or a future time. They can even pay on the spot. This reduces pressure on your team and makes the process fast and smooth for clients.

## [Take payments up front](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#take-payments-up-front)

Cal.com integrates with Stripe to let you collect deposits or full payment at the time of booking. This helps prevent no shows and ensures your time is protected.

You can set payment rules based on the type of appointment. For example, require a deposit for longer sessions or take full payment for shorter appointments. Everything is customizable so it fits the way you work.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/vfY735u9KjcOCc84mB2aPAGF5Y.png?width=1146&height=577)

## [Booking links that fit your brand](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#booking-links-that-fit-your-brand)

Your Cal.com booking link can be shared anywhere you engage with clients. Add it to your website, drop it into a DM, or include it in your Instagram bio or Linktree. It works across platforms and devices.

You can also create separate pages for different artists in your shop. Each one can manage their own schedule and service offerings, giving clients a smooth way to choose and book.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/LOAP0XU6cwTMUzm7TipzYDLtdUE.png?width=1110&height=455)

## [Built for how tattoo artists work](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#built-for-how-tattoo-artists-work)

Cal.com gives you control over your schedule without extra admin. It works on mobile, supports calendar integrations, and gives clients a simple and professional way to book with you.

Whether you are running a busy shop or working solo, Cal.com helps you reduce no shows, organize walk-ins, and streamline your day.

## [The bottom line](https://cal.com/blog/tattoo-artist-booking-scheduling-calcom\#the-bottom-line)

You should be focused on your craft, not stuck chasing clients and managing bookings. Cal.com brings everything together with one clean and automated system. From QR codes to payment processing, it is a smarter way to handle your appointments.

If you are ready to simplify your scheduling and protect your time, try [Cal.com](https://cal.com/)

# The benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time

# The benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time

# The benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/L2A0MPsLwwHjju92LVo8wdWlog0.png?width=1216&height=608)

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/L2A0MPsLwwHjju92LVo8wdWlog0.png?width=1216&height=608)

## [The benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time](https://cal.com/blog/the-benefits-of-using-a-calendar-to-schedule-your-time\#the-benefits-of-using-a-calendar-to-schedule-your-time)

Calendars are a lot like salt; they help to enhance the flavor of life. The benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time can be experienced almost instantly. Using a calendar to schedule your time helps to ensure that meetings don't run over and all parties are set up for success. This is great because it allows you to be the most productive, engaged, and innovative version of yourself. However, calendars can be used for so much more than just scheduling time during your workday. Using a calendar to schedule your time is one of the easiest ways to reduce your stress levels and work towards achieving your goals and dreams. This frees up resources, so that you can invest in yourself, your relationships, and experience more of life. Let's take a moment to explore the top three benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/sE544EYEiaqQX4KKuSpBV08.jpg?width=1279&height=736)

## [**Number One**](https://cal.com/blog/the-benefits-of-using-a-calendar-to-schedule-your-time\#number-one)

Using a calendar to schedule your time helps to build and reinforce a habit of mindfulness. Instead of having goals and ideas floating around in your mind, you're logging them in a concrete way and therefore bringing them out of the realm of thought and into reality hence, creating a habit of mindfulness. This is helpful because it allows you to live more of your life in the present moment, rather than dwelling in the past or ruminating on the future.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/WEW6hrC2q87VMeayHzqyAWUTE.jpg?width=1280&height=853)

## [**Number Two**](https://cal.com/blog/the-benefits-of-using-a-calendar-to-schedule-your-time\#number-two)

Using a calendar to schedule your time is great for your health. Life is busy, and often one of the first things to slip through the cracks is personal care. We often forget to invest in our health when taking care of other matters related to work and family. When you use a calendar to schedule time to the gym, the dentist, or just read a good book, you’re making sure your health isn’t pushed to the side. The simple truth of the matter is that if you don't schedule the time, you’re more likely to deprioritize it.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/QprFbeH3HvP3FFCGaOgboPblqA8.jpg?width=1280&height=831)

## [**Number Three**](https://cal.com/blog/the-benefits-of-using-a-calendar-to-schedule-your-time\#number-three)

Using a calendar to schedule time for your relationships is one of the best ways to show your friends and family how much you care. Every moment of our life, no matter how mundane, is precious, so it means a lot when you commit to sharing that time with others. It might seem like a small thing to schedule a 20-minute conversation once a week with a grandparent, but for them, it's huge; in fact, it might be the highlight of their week.

So, now that we've finished covering the benefits of using a calendar to schedule your time, there's only one thing left to do, put it into action. You can start the process by using a calendar scheduling app like Cal.com.

# The best calendar scheduling apps for small business owners

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/YR54Uj9XSwh60x1vsCrKaVT6RU8.png?width=1216&height=608)

As a small business owner, having a reliable calendar app is vital to help manage your schedule and keep track of appointments and meetings. There are many different options, each with unique features and benefits. Some products come with access to built-in app stores. In contrast, other platforms combine various features usually found as separate services. No matter your needs, there is a calendar scheduling app that can meet them. In this article, we will explore some of the best calendar apps for small business owners, including Cal.com, Amie, Google Calendar, and Doodle.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/lEpRCtelgHwJ7QJFS2ihbvTAzTs.png?width=1700&height=820)

## [Cal.com](https://cal.com/blog/the-best-calendar-scheduling-apps-for-small-business-owners\#cal-com)

Cal.com is an open-source calendar scheduling infrastructure platform. Cal.com is easy to use, white-label friendly, and free for individuals. It can handle everything from collective events to round-robin scheduling and varying hours of operation. Cal.com integrates with your digital calendar of choice and can be used to manage everything from in-person to virtual appointments. Cal.com also comes with a [built-in app store](https://cal.com/blog/category/apps) that supports integration with products like Google Analytics, Zoom, Salesforce, and a whole host of other services. If all that wasn’t enough, we also have options for self-hosting and HIPAA compliance. It’s the ideal choice for any small business owner who prioritizes transparency, customization, innovation, and data security.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/snL6oozB0P7Yl8EcugoqViO4jLg.png?width=1824&height=913)

## [Amie](https://cal.com/blog/the-best-calendar-scheduling-apps-for-small-business-owners\#amie)

Amie is a joyful productivity app that combines the features of a digital calendar, a to-do list, and a customer relationship management system. Amie also supports bookable meeting links and comes with plans for both individuals and teams. The app is Google Calendar compatible and is available on iOS devices. Amie is a great calendar scheduling tool for small businesses prioritizing efficiency and positive vibes. Amie is currently in beta, so if you’re interested in trying it out, click [this link to sign up for the waitlist.](https://amie.so/signup)

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/rOvvpfQUIEWrMLDw4WviwHRR29E.png?width=1834&height=899)

## [Google Calendar](https://cal.com/blog/the-best-calendar-scheduling-apps-for-small-business-owners\#google-calendar)

Google Calendar has been around for a long time, and most people use it. Over the last few years, Google Calendar has grown in capability and applicability. [Google Calendar](https://cal.com/blog/calendly-alternatives-for-google-calendar) now has built integrations for real conferencing via tools like Google Meet. In fact, Google work subscribers can now send and manage appointment booking links via either the appointment slots or appointment schedule (yes, they’re different features). Google Calendar is an excellent choice for any small business owner that already has a Google Work account and doesn’t want to leave the Google ecosystem.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/xKwz7aEl6RSmj4VKtveSFDOs9I.png?width=1787&height=890)

## [Doodle](https://cal.com/blog/the-best-calendar-scheduling-apps-for-small-business-owners\#doodle)

Doodle is primarily known for solving scheduling conundrums by creating time-based polls that people can use to figure out the best state for scheduling a meeting or an event. Recently, the platform has enhanced its offerings by developing its own calendar scheduling app. This means that you can also use Doodle to send out and manage meeting links and polling groups of individuals to identify the most effective date and time. Because of this, doodle is an excellent choice for small businesses that frequently host events with employees, clients, and community members.

As you can see, there are many great calendar apps available to small business owners. Each product listed above comes with its own set of specializations and strengths. Choosing the right calendar app will help you stay organized and productive. This, in turn, will simplify various workflows and improve the level of effectiveness within your business. No matter which calendar app you choose, you are making a choice that will positively impact your bottom line.
